name: Western Digital
window: Q3 FY26 print + intra-quarter · Apr 30 → Jul 28, 2026

events.text: Q3 FY26: revenue $3.3B (+45% YoY), above the top of guide; non-GAAP EPS $2.72 (~2x YoY); non-GAAP GM 50.5% (+1,040bps YoY). Cloud $3.0B (89% of rev, +48% YoY). Volume 222 exabytes (+34% YoY); price per TB +9% YoY. HAMR in qualification with four customers (44TB). LTAs extend into CY2028-2029. Q4 guide: rev $3.65B ±$100M, GM 51-52%, EPS $3.25; dividend +20% to $0.15.

JPM (read from the TMC conference): pricing is the biggest incremental upside — neither WDC nor Seagate tried to temper price-increase expectations; from the current ~+9% QoQ level, 'mid-teens increases in 12 months could be.' WDC is more price-driven (cost declines limited to ~-10%/exabyte) vs Seagate more cost-driven; both reiterated no unit additions (growth only via density).

events.src: Morgan Stanley · Erik Woodring ('HDDs: The Next Leg Higher')
events.text: Pricing upside idea in nearline (Industry View Cautious, but the long thesis is pricing). HDD vendors targeting ~$25/TB blended in CY27 and ~$30 in CY28 vs ~$14.50/TB today; non-LTA customers already paying ~+30% QoQ and NeoCloud spot at $30-35/TB.

Woodring raised numbers 'materially again' on Asia checks: demand broadening from cloud to AI training/inference, humanoids and robots; supply limited to ~30-35% annual exabyte growth, elongating the cycle. WDC CY27/CY28 EPS 'a little over $45 and a little over $70' if the checks hold — sub-10x in CY28. Keeps Seagate as top pick (WDC 1B) since WDC has not yet qualified HAMR and only ramps 44TB in H1 CY27.

Live HDD preview from the published 07-27 note's author, on the morning of the STX print (nothing superseded). The call: "I think we are going to get a pricing-driven beat and raise this quarter… [but] we've tried to kind of keep expectations in check because, at least in my conversations with investors, I felt like expectations have run a little bit rampant." The dispersion, quantified: the company is implying ~3-4% SEQUENTIAL price growth for the June quarter while "some of the higher end of bulls" sit at 8, 10, 12, 14% sequential. Where the upside actually comes from is uncontracted volume — from an Asia trip last month, "everyone that is not on an HDD contract is seeing significant price hikes. We're talking 30, 40 and in some cases 50%," with the sizing caveat kept ("a smaller part of both Seagate and WD's business. Nevertheless, it should have a decent impact this quarter"). He restates the HDD-is-not-memory separation verbally: ~50% gross margins with 70-80% incremental, "nowhere close to peak," revenue growth accelerating over the next five quarters, and no new capacity or supply visible "one, two, three years" out in a 3-player structure with no Chinese competitors. Host Sean adds a human-capital barrier to new supply, net-new: "anybody below 40 years old has no idea how to make hard disk drives anymore. These companies are sending engineers to universities to teach how to make these things." The single most useful line for this name is the cross-name one, delivered on STX's print morning and a week before WDC's 8/5 AMC: "we'll see what happens with Seagate tonight. And obviously Western Digital is next Wednesday. I don't expect a lot of differentiation between the two of them when it comes to what they report or how they guide. Should be a nice beat and raise and the question is just how much pricing do we get this quarter?" — which resolves an ambiguity the page has carried since April: MS's STX-over-WDC ranking is a roadmap/tactical call on the HAMR calendar, not an expectation of a better quarter or guide at STX. The non-LTA repricing is also more WDC-relevant, since WDC is the price-driven name of the pair.

cells: Pulled forward to H1 2026, ramp H1 2027
